description: Edit fields on an existing task. Only set_title changes the task id (id_changed/previous_id report it); every other field leaves the id unchanged. skip_occurrence advances a recurring task's next occurrence WITHOUT completing it (no status flip, no completion date) — mutually exclusive with set_status and set_recurrence/clear_recurrence. set_parent reparents the task under another task (its FIRST child; inline tasks move their whole subtree, a TaskNotes task's parent is written in the vault's configured encoding — the parent's id in a parent field, or a wikilink in projects) and clear_parent promotes it to root level — the two are mutually exclusive, and neither changes the task id. A checklist item in a TaskNotes task's body (body parsing on) is a subtask of that task because of where its line sits: clearing its parent, outdenting a top-level item, or parenting it to a task outside that note is refused with 'parent is implied by location' (move_task moves it out instead). set_description replaces a task file's body text but KEEPS its subtasks with their notes and nested subtasks: subtasks match by exact title at the same level, and anything the new text does not carry is put back (a reworded subtask counts as new, so the old one stays). set_body replaces the whole body and is refused when that would drop a subtask or subtask note, unless replace_subtasks:true is also passed; that is the way to rename or remove subtasks. Without replace_subtasks:true, both refuse a text that drops a code or comment block holding a task, or that leaves a code, comment or raw HTML block open. set_props takes {key: JSON value}, typed as add_task's props; a value that does not fit a defined property (a select value outside its options) is still written and reported in warnings. remove_projects matches a stored project however it is spelled (v3.1.0 = [[v3.1.0]]); a path (Work/Clients) matches only that path, and a bare name that fits two notes is refused. Every remove that removed nothing is listed in unmatched_removals (with a warning), so check it is empty. set_recurrence/clear_recurrence on a recurring SERIES PARENT (a task whose limited recurrence is written out as #recur-… instances) rewrites the series: its future todo instances are removed and new ones are written, possibly in other notes; finished and started instances stay, and a todo instance with a nested task keeps its place. On an instance that is not the parent only that task changes (a warning says so). The warnings report the counts, and dry_run:true reports them without writing.

add_depends_on.description:
Task ids to add as dependencies. A task's `id` from any record works:
it is written as the target's durable user id, minted if the target
has none.

append_note.description:
APPEND to the existing TaskNotes body (a running report log) rather
than replace it — existing lines (incl. folded body-subtasks) are
preserved, separated from the appended block by a blank line.
TaskNotes-only. Mutually exclusive with `set_description`/`set_body`.

assign_id.description:
Vault-wide task ids (2026-08-05) — mint a stable `user_task_id`
(`🆔`/`id::`/`id:`) if this task doesn't already have one; a no-op
when it does (mint-if-missing never overwrites). Mutually exclusive
with `set_id`.

clear_cancelled.description: Clear the cancelled date. Mutually exclusive with `set_cancelled`.

clear_due.description: Clear the due date. Mutually exclusive with `set_due`.

clear_duration_minutes.description: Clear the duration. Mutually exclusive with `set_duration_minutes`.

clear_parent.description:
Phase 6.2 — promote the task to root level (clear its parent). For
an INLINE task this moves it (and its subtree) out to indent 0;
for a task file it strips the parent value from BOTH encodings —
the `parent:` key and the `projects` entry — whatever the vault
is configured to write. Mutually exclusive with `set_parent`.

clear_scheduled.description: Clear the scheduled date. Mutually exclusive with `set_scheduled`.

idempotency_key.description:
Run this call at most once: a retry with the same key (after a
timeout, say) returns what the first call did instead of running
again (`idempotency.replayed: true`; `still_holds` says whether later
changes overtook it). A new JSON-RPC id does not make a retry new.
Keys belong to this device; the same key for a different request is
refused.

replace_subtasks.description:
Let `set_body` drop the subtasks it leaves out. Only valid with
`set_body`.

set_body.description:
Replace a task file's WHOLE body, subtasks included. Refused when the
new body would drop existing subtasks or their note lines (matched as
for `set_description`; the error names how many)
unless `replace_subtasks` is true; use `set_description` to change
only the text. On an inline task this is `set_description`.
Mutually exclusive with `set_description` and `append_note`.

set_cancelled.description: Date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` to include a time of day. On an update a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` moves the calendar day and keeps any time already on the field; a trailing `T` (`2026-02-01T`) drops the time. Empty/omitted leaves it unset.

set_description.description:
Set the description: a task file's body text (`\n`-separated); an
inline task's note. A task file's body subtasks are KEPT, with their
notes and nested subtasks: subtasks match by exact title at the same
level, and whatever the new text does not carry goes back (the rest
of a carried subtask's subtree under it, unmatched ones after the
text). A reworded subtask is a new one, so the old one is kept too;
to rename or remove a subtask use `set_body` with `replace_subtasks`.
Empty string clears the text and keeps the subtasks. Mutually
exclusive with `set_body` and `append_note`.

set_due.description: Date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` to include a time of day. On an update a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` moves the calendar day and keeps any time already on the field; a trailing `T` (`2026-02-01T`) drops the time. Empty/omitted leaves it unset.

set_duration_minutes.description:
Set the estimated duration in minutes. Mutually exclusive with
`clear_duration_minutes`.

set_id.description:
Vault-wide task ids (2026-08-05) — set `user_task_id` to this EXACT
value. Errors if another task in the vault already carries it.

set_on_completion.description:
Set the on-completion action (`keep`, `delete`, or `archive`) — what
happens to the task's line when it's next completed.

set_parent.description:
Phase 6.2 — reparent the task under the task with this corpus id
(it becomes the new parent's FIRST child). For an INLINE task this
moves the whole subtree + re-indents; for a task file it writes
the parent in the encoding this vault is configured for — the
parent's id in a `parent:` key, or a wikilink in `projects` — and
removes the old value from both, so a file never carries two.
`get_dialect` reports which encoding that is. A reparent does NOT
change the task id. Mutually exclusive with `clear_parent`.

set_priority.description: Priority token. One of: highest, high, medium, low, lowest, none (`none` clears any priority). Custom per-vault display names also resolve (read them with the get_dialect tool).

set_props.description:
Custom properties to set (`key` → `value`). Keys are a letter, number or
emoji in any script, then letters, numbers, `_`, `-` and spaces, with a
letter or emoji somewhere (`段階`, `ticket-ref`, `1on1`).
Values are JSON, typed as `add_task`'s `props`: `null` writes an
empty value, `""` or a blank string that text, an array a list, an
object a map (task files only), and any other string reads as on the
CLI (`"42"` a number, `"\"42\""` text, `"a,b"` a list).

set_scheduled.description: Date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` to include a time of day. On an update a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` moves the calendar day and keeps any time already on the field; a trailing `T` (`2026-02-01T`) drops the time. Empty/omitted leaves it unset.

set_start.description: Date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` to include a time of day. On an update a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` moves the calendar day and keeps any time already on the field; a trailing `T` (`2026-02-01T`) drops the time. Empty/omitted leaves it unset.

set_status.description: Status token. One of the canonical values: todo, done, cancelled, in_progress, on_hold, planned, deferred, blocked, someday, ready. Custom per-vault display names also resolve (read them with the get_dialect tool). Default `todo` on create; a raw set on create stamps no completion date.

skip_occurrence.description:
Phase 6.4 — skip a single recurrence occurrence WITHOUT
completing it (no status flip, no completion date, no
onCompletion fire). `None` = no skip requested.

- `Some("YYYY-MM-DD")` = skip THAT SPECIFIC INSTANCE. The task
  advances by exactly ONE occurrence, even if the result is still
  in the past — you named an instance, so instances you did not
  name are left alone.
- `Some("")` = skip requested with no explicit date. Defaults to
  the task's own anchor (scheduled → due → start) AND advances
  past today, so a stale series comes back with a FUTURE
  occurrence in one call rather than one call per missed period.
  Note this DISCARDS the missed occurrences — inline tasks have
  nowhere to record a skip. Name a date if you want one step.

Mutually exclusive with `set_status` and
`set_recurrence`/`clear_recurrence`.

space.description:
Archive with this saved space's (id or name, as `list_spaces`
reports it) archive folder or file rather than the one the task's
own spaces select. With `set_status: "done"`: applies when the completion fires an onCompletion
archive. An unknown space is refused.

name: update_task
